report:
Your results are about what your rating predicts: you scored 50% against an expected 49% [F1], and the data shows no clear weakness.

## Biggest weaknesses

**No clear weakness showed up.** You made 557 blunders where the model expected 566.9, which is 0.98 times expected (90% interval 0.92 to 1.05) [F2]. No opening family is a clear problem once you adjust for opponent rating and sample size [F8]. The evidence for any single weakness is thin, so treat the points below as things to keep an eye on, not proven problems.

- **The middlegame is where most of your points slip away.** You blunder on 6.6% of middlegame moves, the same rate as your opponents [F10]. That is still about double your rate in the opening (3.1%) [F9] and endgame (3.1%) [F11]. One example is 38...Qh2+, which lost 88 win% when the engine preferred Bf6 [F16] (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186706648876). **What to do:** before each check or capture, ask what your opponent's best reply is.
- **Single moves that lose the game.** 7...h5 lost 89 win% when the engine preferred Nxg4 [F15] (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186801191354). In an endgame, 43...Kh7 lost 93 win% when Qxf4+ was available [F14] (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186801649660). In both games you missed a forcing capture or check. **What to do:** go through every check and capture for both sides before you move.

## What's working

- **You handle low time well.** With under 10% of your clock left, you made 75 blunders against 81.8 expected [F3]. With 10-30% left, it was 61 against 74.0 [F4]. Both intervals include 1 [F3][F4], so this isn't proven, but time pressure is clearly not hurting you.
- **Your Queen's Gambit and Benoni games as White.** In the Queen's Gambit as White you scored 58% against 50% expected [F6], with a median eval of +0.9 after move 12 [F12]. Against the Benoni as White you scored 70% in 10 games [F7]. Both are rated "possible strength."

## Training plan

- Do Lichess middlegame puzzles every day: https://lichess.org/training/middlegame [F17].
- Practise spotting hanging pieces: https://lichess.org/training/hangingPiece [F18].
- Replay the three games linked above. For each one, write down the check or capture you missed.
- Keep playing the Queen's Gambit, and spend your study time on the plans for moves 13-25 [F12]. In those moves you lose 5.1 win% per move, the same as your overall average [F12], so that's where your good openings could turn into more wins.

facts.text: Across 300 games (average rating 1703), you scored 50% versus 49% expected from ratings (+1 points).

A blunder-risk model trained only on your opponents' moves (players of similar rating) expected 566.9 blunders in your 12269 moves given how hard the positions were; you made 557, 0.98 times the expected count (90% interval 0.92 to 1.05).

With under 10% of the clock left, you made 75 blunders in 1407 moves versus 81.8 expected (0.92 times expected, 90% interval 0.75 to 1.11). Treat a band as different from expected only if its interval excludes 1.

With 10-30% of the clock left, you made 61 blunders in 1653 moves versus 74.0 expected (0.82 times expected, 90% interval 0.66 to 1.02). Treat a band as different from expected only if its interval excludes 1.

With over 30% of the clock left, you made 421 blunders in 9209 moves versus 411.1 expected (1.02 times expected, 90% interval 0.94 to 1.11). Treat a band as different from expected only if its interval excludes 1.
Queen's Gambit as White: 52 games, scored 58% versus 50% expected. Rating-adjusted gap after shrinkage: +3 points (90% interval -2 to +10). Verdict: possible strength.
Benoni Defense as White: 10 games, scored 70% versus 49% expected. Rating-adjusted gap after shrinkage: +3 points (90% interval -3 to +12). Verdict: possible strength.
No opening family shows a weakness that is clear after adjusting for opponent rating, sample size and the number of openings checked.

In the opening you lose an average of 3.4 win% per move, with a blunder (a drop of 20 win% or more) on 3.1% of moves (3591 moves analysed). Your opponents: 3.3 win% per move, blunders on 2.8% of moves.

In the middlegame you lose an average of 5.1 win% per move, with a blunder (a drop of 20 win% or more) on 6.6% of moves (4933 moves analysed). Your opponents: 5.1 win% per move, blunders on 6.6% of moves.

In the endgame you lose an average of 2.9 win% per move, with a blunder (a drop of 20 win% or more) on 3.1% of moves (3745 moves analysed). Your opponents: 2.7 win% per move, blunders on 3.2% of moves.
In your Queen's Gambit games as White, the engine eval after move 12 had a median of +0.9 pawns for you; in moves 13-25 you lost 5.1 win% per move, versus 5.1 across all your games.
In your Benoni Defense games as White, the engine eval after move 12 had a median of +0.5 pawns for you; in moves 13-25 you lost 4.7 win% per move, versus 5.1 across all your games.
